projectTitle: Starase Atlas — Atlas-BRIDGE, Atlas-COMPASS and Atlas-EDGE for enzyme discovery
tagline: Given a target reaction and limited experimental resources, which enzyme candidates should a researcher test first?
summary: NJU-China built a three-part platform around one decision: which enzyme to test next. Atlas-BRIDGE (Broad Retrieval with Inference-Driven Gated Experts) is a dual-tower contrastive retrieval model that will rank any protein it can encode, then lets specialist 'expert' models and two kinds of memory nudge that ranking only where their evidence genuinely applies; Atlas-COMPASS is a natural-language agent front end that resolves entities before it computes anything; Atlas-EDGE is a MySQL/graph knowledge base of compound nodes and enzyme edges built from UniProt, Rhea and ChEBI. The model's recommendation was then taken to the bench: M5AW86 was predicted and confirmed to convert FPP to beta-farnesene by GC-MS, TLC and 1H NMR against empty-vector controls. It won Best Software & AI Project and was nominated for Best Model.

dry.frameworks: Atlas-BRIDGE is a machine-learning information-retrieval model, not a kinetic one, and its central design idea is worth copying regardless of domain: separate *eligibility to be ranked* from *availability of evidence*. The base model ('Broad') is a two-tower encoder — one tower for protein sequence, one for reaction transformation — trained with a multi-positive contrastive objective that respects the many-to-many nature of enzyme data, L_MP = lambda*L_R2E + (1-lambda)*L_E2R, where each directional loss sums over the full set of known positives rather than treating a single pair as the truth. Because an unrecorded enzyme-reaction pair is not a true negative, they apply positive-unlabeled (PU) learning plus sequence-cluster masking to decide which pairs are even admitted for contrast, and because experimental screening only tests the top of a list they add an explicit head-ranking hinge, L_head = softplus(n_K - p* + m), pushing the best positive above the K-th admissible negative, with hard negatives mined from the candidates the current model confuses most. The final score is additive and auditable: S = S_Broad + alpha_LT*Delta_LT + alpha_epi*Delta_epi + sum_k g_k*Delta_k. The Gated Experts are plug-in models carrying functional, structural/mechanistic or family/domain evidence; each must publish candidate-wise scores *and an availability mask*, has its applicability gate, normalisation and maximum correction magnitude locked on separate validation data before any external test, and reverts exactly to the prior ranking wherever its evidence is missing — so absent data is never silently read as a low score. Long-term memory replays the training-cutoff catalytic graph at inference, projecting 16 annotated protein neighbours and 8 annotated reaction neighbours back into the Broad space with query-conditioned permission weights fitted on 5,216 annotated development associations, and it only re-sorts the top 1,000 Broad candidates. Episodic memory handles positives that appear *after* the training cutoff (new curation, new assays, a collaborator's private hit) without retraining anything: each support is encoded in the frozen Broad space and combined by parameter-free attention, a_i = softmax(zscore(q^T s_i)), m_epi = sum a_i s_i, with authority scaled by support count, internal coherence and conflict with the baseline; positives already in the training graph are stripped out first to prevent double-counting with long-term memory. Atlas-COMPASS wraps this in a DeepSeek-API-driven agent that first resolves every reaction, protein and compound in a plain-language question to a Rhea / UniProt / ChEBI record and shows a confirmation card the user must approve before anything is computed, then plans the retrieval, and can additionally run thermodynamic Max-min Driving Force analysis and E. coli iML1515 genome-scale flux checks on candidate pathways when asked.
dry.dataviz: The visual argument is carried by the evaluation figures rather than by decoration. Benchmark comparisons are plotted as grouped MRR / Hit@10 / Hit@20 bars against EnzymeCAGE on two external test sets, with the harder Orphan-335 set shown alongside Enzyme-405 so the reader sees where the gain is largest. The four-configuration study is drawn as a controlled 2x2 (reference, coverage-only, ranker-only, complete system) in both retrieval directions, so the figure itself separates 'we found more candidates' from 'we ranked them better'. Ablation panels remove one evidence block at a time in both directions. Seed-count sensitivity is shown both as performance-versus-number-of-positive-seeds line plots under two evaluation protocols (random-positive and the much stricter protein-cluster-cold) and as grouped Hit@3/10/20 bars for one, two and three seeds. The model page also renders the architecture itself — dual-tower geometry, anchored reranking that visibly protects the base order, and query-level gating of each expert — as labelled schematics, and the five development cycles are laid out as a descending staircase so the reader walks the DBTL history. Atlas-EDGE's own interface is the other half of the dataviz: a hand-built SVG graph in which compounds are nodes and enzymes are directional edges, with composite edges that collapse multiple enzymes between two compounds and expand on click, click-through compound and enzyme info cards, zoom, drag, filtering, path highlighting and URL-synced view state.
dry.datascience: Evaluation is the strongest part of this project and is unusually self-sceptical. External benchmarking used the EnzymeCAGE authors' own test sets under their protocol: 21,505 training-unseen positive relationships ranked over the full encodable universe of 185,918 protein candidates (11,081 reaction candidates in the reverse direction). Reported gains: Enzyme-405 MRR +16.0% and Hit@10 +4.55pp; Orphan-335 MRR +44.0%, Hit@10 +17.32pp, Hit@20 +18.51pp. Four ablation studies follow, including a difficulty-balanced re-aggregation that freezes every prediction, candidate set and rank and changes *only* the averaging — giving equal weight to seen, protein-cold, reaction-cold and double-cold exposure classes and then to the graph-degree strata within each — explicitly to stop frequent, highly connected, easy relations dominating a micro-average. Domain experts were tested only on queries where they are applicable, with deterministic family held-out splits for P450 and phosphatase and a frozen semantic applicability gate selecting 18 of 1,042 strict double-cold queries for terpene synthases; gains were P450 MRR 0.0394 to 0.0503, phosphatase 0.3012 to 0.3077, TPS 0.1225 to 0.3114 with Hit@10 11.11% to 33.33%, candidate sets and core scores held fixed. Wet-lab closure: M5AW86 was recommended for FPP to beta-farnesene and confirmed by a converging evidence chain (differential GC-MS peak at ~5.5 min with base peak m/z 69, fragments at 41/81/93/107/121/135 and a low-abundance molecular ion at m/z 204; TLC spots absent from empty-vector controls; 1H NMR olefinic signals at delta 6.3-6.4 and 5.0-5.3 ppm matched to a literature reference). They also publish a disconfirmation: for D9XD61 the model predicted (+)-T-muurolol but the isolated product was identified as 7-epi-alpha-eudesmol, and they say so. Preliminary GC-MS hit rate was 7 of 14 recommended candidates (50%). The interface discipline matches: the 0-100 displayed model score is explicitly documented as 'not a catalytic success rate', not activity or yield, not comparable across retrieval routes, and a high rank means 'deserves priority verification, not that it has been biologically proven'; 'unknown' in a compatibility cell means missing records, not incompatibility.
dry.software: Both instruments are Apache 2.0 open source in the official iGEM GitLab repository, deployable with git clone plus bash scripts/bootstrap.sh, setup_release.sh --download and --check, then manage.sh configure-key / start / status. Linux with Python 3.12 is the validated environment, ~5 GiB for model assets, WSL2 for Windows, macOS explicitly flagged as not validated — and crucially no GPU is required, since validation and inference run on CPU. The DeepSeek API key is stored in a git-ignored runtime directory and the docs tell deployers to put the service behind HTTPS with access control, rate limiting, log monitoring and API quotas, and to explain how external model services handle data. Atlas-EDGE is a full production stack: React + TypeScript + Vite front end (hand-drawn SVG graph, History API URL sync, localStorage session persistence, AbortController to cancel stale searches), FastAPI + Uvicorn + Pydantic + async SQLAlchemy/aiomysql backend on a /api/v1 prefix, MySQL 8.0.46, a four-round UniProt REST crawl plus Rhea SPARQL and ChEBI flat files, pandas/RDKit ETL into entity and association tables with a unified sha1-keyed search index, local NCBI BLAST+ (blastp/makeblastdb, run in a thread with a mutex guarding database construction and an sha1 cache key), Ketcher for draw-a-molecule structure search, and DeepSolNet run locally with original weights to generate per-protein solubility scores used as a search filter.

good.publicEngagement: Nine primary-school lessons from March to July 2026 (five plant lessons, four summer science lessons), each treated as its own Design-Build-Test-Learn unit: Design fixed audience and objectives, Build made slides and materials, Test watched what pupils actually explained and where they needed help, Learn turned the observed problems into changes to the next lesson. From that they distilled SPARK as a reusable design and review lens — See, Probe, Ask, Record and Respond, Keep improving — and then applied it back onto their secondary-school intro and lab teaching and their public science conversations at Starlight Market. The handover is concrete: slides, activity materials, a lesson design checklist, guidelines for experimental and simulation activities, a feedback and evaluation form, and 'SPARK-Edu Skill', an AI-assisted guide that encodes their principles, workflow and examples so a future education team can adapt rather than restart.
good.ihp: Human Practices is presented as evidence that changed the build, with a counted audit trail: 24 evidence records, 6 stakeholder lenses, 4 design shifts, 3 intended influence pathways, across academic (8), iGEM and user (4), industry (5), technology transfer (3), safety (2) and education contacts. The four shifts are stated as before/after pairs: from a black-box compatibility score to explicit experimental prioritisation; from searching known pairs to open exploration with uncertainty; from ranked names only to explainable recommendations; from a post-hoc warning to responsibility by design. The origin is traceable: in November 2025 Jing Shi pointed out that a promising enzyme record may behave differently in a new host, Fei Zhou described the preparatory work caused by scattered information, and Long Wang warned that sequence similarity is not function — which is why the platform separates recorded associations (the factual layer) from model candidates (the prediction layer) in every view. The team also took on the dual-use question directly: if an AI tool makes finding functional enzymes easier, which questions should it decline to answer lightly, how should high-risk queries be handled, and what may private data be used for.
good.realWorld: The entrepreneurship case is for a screening *service* rather than another database: computational screening carried through to wet-lab validation so the customer receives a confirmed candidate, with the pipeline and its documentation left behind as a reusable toolkit and the methods and data kept public. Numbers are stated with their baselines: enzyme-to-reaction accuracy 15.32% (up from 8.47% in the team's own historical runs), a 1.92x top-20 hit rate against CLIPZyme (15.97% vs 8.33%) over 166,202 benchmark candidates, a 50% preliminary GC-MS hit rate (7 of 14), an estimated core enterprise TAM of RMB 14.42M annually in the baseline forecast, and a proposed tiered price range of RMB 4.3k to 319.5k per year from Academic to Enterprise Advanced. They are candid that the current demo only accepts target reactions and candidate proteins and returns rankings, with traceability, version management and full decision support still to come. The stated audiences are research labs (inspectable enzyme discovery), the iGEM community (reflective HP practice) and the bio-manufacturing ecosystem (governed, compatible pilots).

images.caption: Atlas-BRIDGE architecture: a shared dual-tower retrieval geometry that will score any encodable protein or reaction, with query-level gated experts and dual (long-term graph plus episodic) memory applying additive corrections only inside their valid scope.

The Broad Retrieval dual-tower architecture for bidirectional enzyme-reaction ranking: one tower encodes protein sequence, the other the reaction transformation, trained with a multi-positive contrastive loss plus a head-ranking constraint so the top of the list — the part experiments actually test — is sharpened.

Performance as a function of the number of positive seeds, plotted under two evaluation protocols — random-positive and the much stricter protein-cluster-cold — so the reader can see how much of the apparent gain survives when close homologs of the known positives are withheld.

Query-level gating of the functional, structural/mechanistic, family/domain and memory experts. Each expert must emit an availability mask as well as scores, and reverts exactly to the prior ranking wherever its evidence is missing, so absent data is never read as a low score.

gemsTakeaway: Make every model output carry an availability mask, so 'we have no evidence about this candidate' and 'this candidate scores badly' are never the same number — and separate the factual layer (what a database records) from the prediction layer (what your model guesses) in every table and figure you publish. Then re-aggregate your headline metric with equal weight across difficulty strata to check your result is not just the easy cases.
